fullPassage:
Did you know that February 2nd is World Wetlands Day? Some may wonder whether wetlands are important enough to celebrate every year. They may think wetlands are useless and unpleasant places, but actually they are unique ecosystems that must be protected because they provide numerous benefits to both the environment and humans. For example, Upo is Korea's largest untouched wetland, covering an area as big as 210 soccer fields. First of all, Upo is a habitat for a number of threatened and endangered species. To name a few, there is the rare gasiyeon and the ttaogi, a bird which is nearly extinct. Furthermore, Upo prevents floods by absorbing water during the rainy season of July and August, and it supplies adequate water to local farmers during droughts. Like Upo, there are other wetlands in the world that help the environment and humans around them. Let's take a look at some of them.

The Camargue / France
The Camargue is a region in southern France where the Rhône River meets the Mediterranean Sea, just a few miles from the city of Arles. It functions as a natural sponge, absorbing and gradually releasing surface water such as rain, groundwater, and floodwater. Its ability to hold water aids in flood control. The Camargue is also an excellent place to observe more than 400 species of birds. Due to the fact that wetlands and lakes cover 35% of the area, the Camargue is an ideal place for flocks of birds to feed and cool off. The exotic pink flamingo is one of the most famous species found there. The area is also known historically for its white horses. The Camargue horses are a special breed, said to be one of the world's oldest, and they have spent thousands of years living in the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted to its salty wetlands. They have become powerful and strong as a result of surviving in the Camargue, where only reeds, thick grasses, and weeds are available. If you have ever seen a magnificent image of horses running through water, it is very likely that they are Camargue horses from this area.

The Everglades / USA
The Everglades is a wetland that stretches from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. It functions as a "biological supermarket." Many birds and mammal species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter, particularly during the migration and breeding seasons. For example, the Florida panther has flourished in the Everglades. It was nearly extinct in 1995, with only a dozen adults estimated in the wild. But the whole population in the Everglades National Park had recovered to about 230 by 2017.

What is more, the Everglades is the only place where American crocodiles and American alligators coexist. These animals typically inhabit different ecosystems: crocodiles live in salt water, whereas alligators live in fresh water. However, they are found living together where fresh water from Lake Okeechobee meets the salt water of Florida Bay. Besides, the Everglades provides drinking water to people in Florida, with one out of every three people relying on the Everglades for drinking water. Unless the Everglades is preserved, millions of people will suffer from a shortage of drinking water.

The Sudd / South Sudan
The Sudd wetland is the largest wetland in Africa, sustained by the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria in Uganda. In the Sudd, there are many endangered mammal species, including African elephants and antelopes. Additionally, one million people rely on the wetland for a living, primarily through cattle herding. For example, during the dry season, nomadic people move deeper into the wetland and build seasonal homes on naturally occurring islands to feed their herds like sheep, cows, and goats and catch the abundant fish. The name "Sudd" comes from an Arabic word for "barriers," and the wetland historically protected the people from invaders. The Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans spent centuries searching for the starting point of the Nile River. Nero, the emperor of the Roman empire, sent the military to explore the White Nile in 61 AD, but his soldiers were unable to proceed beyond the Sudd.

Wetlands, no matter where they are found, clearly provide habitats for a variety of endangered plant and animal species, as well as humans. Unfortunately, wetlands are currently under threat. The Camargue, for example, is decreasing as sea levels rise due to climate change. The Everglades used to be much larger, but due to agriculture and urban development, less than half of the historic Everglades remains today. The Sudd has been contaminated by oil spills from oil extraction activities. It is estimated that 64% of the world's wetlands have disappeared. Now that we understand the importance of wetlands in maintaining our ecosystems, we should consider ways to live without destroying the wetlands that provide valuable benefits to animals, plants, and humans.

ch: 카마르그는 해수면 상승으로 면적이 줄고 있다.
에버글레이즈의 역사적 면적 중 절반 미만이 현재 남아 있다.

det.korean: ③ 수드의 오염 원인은 기후 변화가 아닌 석유 유출(oil spills)이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 일치: 'decreasing as sea levels rise due to climate change'.

❌ ② 일치: 'less than half of the historic Everglades remains'.

✅ ③ 불일치: 수드 = 석유 유출(oil spills). 기후 변화는 카마르그 원인. ←정답

❌ ④ 일치: '64% of the world's wetlands have disappeared'.
det.tip: 위협 원인 구분: 카마르그=기후변화, 에버글레이즈=농업/도시, 수드=석유유출.

questions.passage: ①The Sudd wetland is the largest wetland in Africa, sustaining by the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria in Uganda. ②In the Sudd, there are many endangered mammal species, including African elephants and antelopes. ③Additionally, one million people rely on the wetland for a living, primarily through cattle herding. ④The Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans spent centuries searching for the starting point of the Nile River.

markers.②: In the Sudd, there are many endangered mammal species, including African elephants and antelopes.
markers.③: Additionally, one million people rely on the wetland for a living, primarily through cattle herding.
markers.④: The Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans spent centuries searching for the starting point of the Nile River.

questions.stem: 다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 부분이 포함된 문장을 고르시오.

det.korean: ① sustaining → sustained: 습지가 유지'되는' 것이므로 과거분사(수동) 필요.
det.analysis:
❌ ① sustaining → sustained: 'sustained by ~'(~에 의해 유지되는). 수동 의미이므로 과거분사 필요. ←정답

✅ ② 어법 정상: there are + 복수명사 + including ~.

✅ ③ 어법 정상: rely on ~ for a living, through cattle herding.

✅ ④ 어법 정상: spent + 기간 + V-ing. searching for ~.
det.tip: sustained by(~에 의해 유지되는) = 과거분사(수동). sustaining = 현재분사(능동) — 의미 부적절.

questions.passage: The Everglades is a wetland that stretches from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. It functions as a "biological supermarket." Many birds and mammal species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter, particularly during the migration and breeding seasons. For example, the Florida panther has flourished in the Everglades. It was nearly extinct in 1995, with only a dozen adults estimated in the wild. But the whole population in the Everglades National Park had recovered to about 230 by 2017.
questions.stem:
Q: 에버글레이즈에서 플로리다 표범의 개체 수 변화를 본문에서 찾아 영어로 완성하시오. (영어로) (5단어)
→ The whole population had _____ _____ _____ _____ _____.

det.korean: 플로리다 표범의 전체 개체 수가 2017년까지 약 230마리로 회복(recovered to about 230 by)되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ recovered to about 230 by: 원문 'the whole population had recovered to about 230 by 2017'.
→ 1995년 약 12마리에서 2017년 약 230마리로 회복.
det.tip: recover to ~ = ~까지 회복하다. a dozen(약 12마리) → 230마리.

questions.passage:
The Sudd / South Sudan
The Sudd wetland is the largest wetland in Africa, sustained by the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria in Uganda. In the Sudd, there are many endangered mammal species, including African elephants and antelopes. Additionally, one million people rely on the wetland for a living, primarily through cattle herding. For example, during the dry season, nomadic people move deeper into the wetland and build seasonal homes on naturally occurring islands to feed their herds like sheep, cows, and goats and catch the abundant fish. The name "Sudd" comes from an Arabic word for "barriers," and the wetland historically protected the people from invaders.
questions.stem:
Q: 수드 습지가 역사적으로 수행한 역할을 본문에서 찾아 영어로 완성하시오. (영어로) (4단어)
→ The wetland historically _____ _____ _____ _____.

det.korean: 수드 습지는 역사적으로 사람들을 침략자로부터 보호(protected the people from)했다.
det.analysis:
✅ protected the people from: 원문 'the wetland historically protected the people from invaders'.
→ 습지가 장벽 역할을 하여 침략자로부터 주민을 보호함.
det.tip: protect A from B = A를 B로부터 보호하다.

questions.passage: Did you know that February 2nd is World Wetlands Day? Some may wonder whether wetlands are important enough to celebrate every year. They may think wetlands are useless and unpleasant places, but actually they are unique ecosystems that must be protected because they provide numerous benefits to both the environment and humans. For example, Upo is Korea's largest untouched wetland, covering an area as big as 210 soccer fields. First of all, Upo is a habitat for a number of threatened and endangered species. To name a few, there is the rare gasiyeon and the ttaogi, a bird which is nearly extinct. Furthermore, Upo prevents floods by absorbing water during the rainy season of July and August, and it supplies adequate water to local farmers during droughts.
questions.stem:
위 글에서, 우포가 우기에 수행하는 기능을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (영어로) (2단어)
→ Upo _____ _____ by absorbing water during the rainy season.

det.korean: 우포는 우기에 물을 흡수하여 홍수를 예방(prevents floods)한다.
det.analysis:
✅ prevents floods: 원문 'Upo prevents floods by absorbing water during the rainy season'.
→ 우기(장마철)에 물을 흡수하여 홍수를 방지하는 기능.
det.tip: prevent floods = 홍수를 예방/방지하다. by absorbing = 흡수함으로써.

questions.passage: Wetlands, no matter where they are found, clearly provide habitats for a variety of endangered plant and animal species, as well as humans. Unfortunately, wetlands are currently under threat. The Camargue, for example, is decreasing as sea levels rise due to climate change. The Everglades used to be much larger, but due to agriculture and urban development, less than half of the historic Everglades remains today. The Sudd has been contaminated by oil spills from oil extraction activities. It is estimated that 64% of the world's wetlands have disappeared. Now that we understand the importance of wetlands in maintaining our ecosystems, we should consider ways to live without destroying the wetlands that provide valuable benefits to animals, plants, and humans.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 농업 발전이 자연 생태계에 기여하는 방식
습지 보존의 필요성과 습지가 직면한 위협

det.korean: 주제: 습지 보존의 필요성과 습지가 직면한 위협.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 습지의 종류/특성: 분류가 아닌 위협과 보존 촉구.

❌ ② 기후 변화/해수면: 카마르그 일부 원인일 뿐.

❌ ③ 농업이 기여: 농업은 습지 축소 원인. 기여가 아님.

✅ ④ 보존 필요성 + 위협: 각 습지의 위협 원인 + 'should consider ways to live without destroying'. ←정답
det.tip: 글 전체 핵심: 습지가 위협받고 있으므로 보존해야 한다.

questions.passage: Did you know that February 2nd is World Wetlands Day? Some may wonder whether wetlands are important enough to celebrate every year. They may think wetlands are useless and unpleasant places, but actually they are unique ecosystems that must be protected because they provide numerous benefits to both the environment and humans. For example, Upo is Korea's largest untouched wetland, covering an area as big as 210 soccer fields. First of all, Upo is a habitat for a number of threatened and endangered species. To name a few, there is the rare gasiyeon and the ttaogi, a bird which is nearly extinct. Furthermore, Upo prevents floods by absorbing water during the rainy season of July and August, and it supplies adequate water to local farmers during droughts. Like Upo, there are other wetlands in the world that help the environment and humans around them. Let's take a look at some of them.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 한국의 우포 습지는 세계에서 가장 큰 습지이다.
습지는 환경과 인간 모두에게 다양한 혜택을 제공하는 보호해야 할 생태계이다.
멸종위기 종을 보호하려면 모든 습지를 관광지로 개발해야 한다.

det.korean: 요지: 습지는 환경과 인간 모두에게 혜택을 제공하는 보호해야 할 생태계.
det.analysis:
❌ ① '세계에서 가장 큰' 아닌 '한국 최대'. 요지 범위도 좁음.

❌ ② '농업 용수에만': 서식지 제공 + 홍수 방지 등 다양한 혜택.

✅ ③ 'unique ecosystems that must be protected' + 'numerous benefits to both the environment and humans' — 글 전체 요지. ←정답

❌ ④ 관광지 개발: 본문에 관광/개발 미언급.
det.tip: 요지 = 글 전체의 핵심 주장. 습지 보호 + 다양한 혜택.

questions.passage:
The Camargue / France
The Camargue is a region in southern France where the Rhône River meets the Mediterranean Sea, just a few miles from the city of Arles. It functions as a natural sponge, absorbing and gradually releasing surface water such as rain, groundwater, and floodwater. Its ability to hold water aids in flood control. The Camargue is also an excellent place to observe more than 400 species of birds. Due to the fact that wetlands and lakes cover 35% of the area, the Camargue is an ideal place for flocks of birds to feed and cool off. The exotic pink flamingo is one of the most famous species found there. The area is also known historically for its white horses. The Camargue horses are a special breed, said to be one of the world's oldest, and they have __________ living in the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted to its salty wetlands.
questions.stem:
다음 한국어 의미에 맞게 빈칸을 영작하시오. (영어로)

"카마르그 말들은 수천 년을 보냈다"
→ they have _______ _______ _______ _______ living in the unique environment.

[조건] (1) of, spent, thousands, years를 모두 사용 (2) (4단어)

det.korean: 카마르그 말들은 수천 년을 보냈다(spent thousands of years).
det.analysis:
spent thousands of years = 수천 년을 보냈다.

• have spent: 현재완료 (과거부터 현재까지 계속).
• thousands of years: 수천 년.
• spend + 시간 + V-ing: ~하며 시간을 보내다.
det.tip: spend + 시간 + V-ing = ~하며 시간을 보내다. thousands of = 수천의.
